newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankans await Gulf War compensation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankans await Gulf War compensation.

text.p: About 70,000 Sri Lankans are eligible for compensation from the U.N. Gulf War reparations body for losses incurred during the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait, a government official said on Wednesday.

"We are not sure how many of our people will receive compensation this time, but the total number eligible is about 70,000," Nissanka Wijeratne, chairman of the Bureau of Foreign Employment, told Reuters.

The U.N. Compensation Commission said on Wednesday it had paid $144 million to 63 governments for distribution to 57,636 people who proved they were forced to leave Kuwait or Iraq or who lost up to $100,000.
The Geneva-based body said the payments were funded by its 30 percent share of revenue for the sale of Iraqi crude oil sold under an "oil-for-food" deal implemented since December.
It said Sri Lankan workers would receive $15.9 million, but did not say how many would immediately be eligible.

A large number of individuals, corporations and governments have filed claims valued at more than $220 billion against Baghdad for losses directly due to Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait and its seven-month occupation.
Wijeratne said Sri Lankan authorities would distribute the money once it was debited to the bureau's account.

The U.N. commission, funded largely by donations and seized Iraqi assets, previously paid out $13.4 million to 3,966 people who had suffered the death of close relatives or serious injury to themselves.
Wijeratne said they included 34 Sri Lankans which received a total of $130,000.
Nearly 600,000 Sri Lankans work in the Middle East, 65 percent of them as housemaids. Their remittances have been the top foreign exchange earner for Sri Lanka for the past five years.
